text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Police will probably question cabinet minsiter Sharansky under warning over alleged ties with Gregory Lerner.
- Reform and Conservative rabbis announce compromise on conversion law.
- Security officials concerned about possible armed confrontation between Palestinians and Jewish settlers.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister, Meridor face off in cabinet.
- Deal set on conversion bill.
- Opposition leader calls on Meridor to bring down government.
- Terrorist escapes from Palestinian Authority custody.
- Generali offers $12 million indemnity fund for Holocaust victims.
- Ministry, Israel Aircraft Industries union try to stop share sale to Lockheed-Martin.
MAARIV
- Finance Minister Meridor: "They've decided to wipe me out".
- Transport minister said Netanyahu confirmed Ariel Sharon would be appointed Finance Minister.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu in message to Assad: We must renew negotiations.
- Netanyahu-Meridor: an unnecessary war.
- Schools on strike.
GLOBES
- Bank of Israel forced to buy $500 million to prevent drop in basket.
- Globes poll: Most people support Bank of Israel's position but like Dan Meridor.
